journal_lines: Chased prey through dense timber. The hunter and the woodcutter moved as one — one flushed, the other cut off the retreat.
Found a clearing mid-chase. The trees came down around the quarry. Efficient.
The forest worked for both of them today. Prey and timber, same ground, same hour.
The prey ran into the timber. The timber fell. The prey was found.
Flushed from the meadow into the trees. Followed with both skills.
A hunt that doubled as a cutting day.
The forest gave both at once. Efficient.
Quarry in the old growth. Took the timber that blocked the approach. Took the quarry.
The forest edges are where both kinds of work overlap. Today was that edge.
Used the axe to clear the approach and the weapon to finish it. One continuous motion.
The prey made the mistake of entering the woodcutter's ground.
Trees and prey, both in the same stand. Neither escaped the clearing.
